bug_semantics: The generic CRUD add handler created a new entity and marshalled attacker-controlled POST data, including an id, into that entity before save. A later guard inspected and removed id from the controller-options array $params, but __massageInput($params) independently rebuilt $input from $this->request->getData(); the attacker-controlled id therefore survived into patchEntity(), allowing an add endpoint to persist an attacker-chosen server-controlled identifier and potentially spoof objects, collide identifiers, or corrupt references.
flaw_origin: Commit 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b first added app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php and its generic add() data flow: on POST it passed $this->request->getData() directly to patchEntity() and then saved the new entity without excluding id. Commit a7348e5266b21f210d0d37eb397dbd52a5302659 later refactored the raw request read into __massageInput($params) without filtering id, and 7159034e9e1b2b9e0f61efeef2acce5651fd756e later added the ineffective unset($params['id']) guard. Those later commits preserved or attempted to mitigate the already-existing flaw; they did not first introduce the vulnerable request-to-entity sink.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author and committer as iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>, contains no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no bot identity, and no other AI-attribution marker; its message is 'new: [CRUD] crud component added' followed only by two ordinary bullet lines.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g5c4-g774-r8rq (API: https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-G5C4-G774-R8RQ) states that Cerebrate before 1.37 allowed id mass assignment in generic CRUD add because id was removed from $params before normalization, while normalized $input still contained it; it identifies https://github.com/cerebrate-project/cerebrate/commit/aff1ca707c8f926d00cda3deb39ff9bf59cdf18e as the fix. In the validated full-history clone, `git diff dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b -- app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php` shows the file added from /dev/null and add() calling patchEntity($data, $this->request->getData()) before save; `git diff --name-status` shows that this BIC changed only that newly added file. `git ls-tree -r --name-only dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71 -- app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php` returns no path, directly proving the vulnerable component and lines absent from the BIC parent. Pickaxe for the raw patchEntity expression returns 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b as its addition, later path/history changes df4937410343d41b397b9088a9d1eb528c1998bf and a7348e5266b21f210d0d37eb397dbd52a5302659, and blame across the pre-fix add() follows the sink back through app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php to 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b. The v0.1 tree still shows app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php:55 passing raw request data to patchEntity(), proving the issue predates the ineffective guard added in 7159034e9e1b2b9e0f61efeef2acce5651fd756e. The direct one-parent fix diff from 09f7351bd124367a1477ea77279b48cb78f04ecb to aff1ca707c8f926d00cda3deb39ff9bf59cdf18e in src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php removes the pre-normalization unset($params['id']) and adds unset($input['id']) immediately after __massageInput() and before patchEntity(). Tag containment places the BIC in v0.1 and every later release; fix containment returns v1.37 and v1.38 but not v1.36, matching the advisory's textual affected boundary (<1.37) and patched boundary (v1.37). The exact BIC object has parent dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71, human author/committer iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>, and no AI trailer or bot marker.
reasoning: The advisory's changed line initially points to 7159034e9e1b2b9e0f61efeef2acce5651fd756e, which introduced the mistaken $params-side id removal, but vulnerability-first history shows that this was only an ineffective mitigation: the generic component had accepted raw request data into a new entity since 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b, and v0.1 already shipped that sink. The a7348e5266b21f210d0d37eb397dbd52a5302659 normalization refactor retained the same attacker-controlled data flow, and 7159034e9e1b2b9e0f61efeef2acce5651fd756e left it intact because it changed $params rather than the normalized request-derived $input. Therefore the smallest source-origin BIC is the one-file component addition 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b, not the later refactor, failed guard, path movement, or fix. Its direct parent contains neither historical nor current-path CRUDComponent.php, satisfying parent-tree absence. The direct fix aff1ca707c8f926d00cda3deb39ff9bf59cdf18e filters id from the actual marshalled input before patching and first appears in v1.37. Because the BIC commit object contains only a human author/committer and ordinary message text with no AI marker, the BIC-only attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
